findings.evidence: Threshold is cited as psd-tools apply_threshold but implemented as lum >= level. psd-tools rounds luminance to the LUT scale and compares strictly against (threshold - 1/255) * (lut-1)/lut * bit_factor, which moves the 8-bit boundary by about half a code value. A pixel with lum 127.6/255 at level 128 is white in psd-tools and black here. The hand test only uses lum 0.6 and 0.3, far from the boundary. The class is Approximate and UNVERIFIED against Photoshop (D5 7), so this is a citation/behaviour mismatch, not a contract break.
findings.remediation: Either implement the cited psd-tools rounding/offset with a boundary test, or reword the citation as a Studio rule

Tile-parallel determinism (par.rs): run_indexed hands out indices in increasing order, so every index below a failing one has been fetched and is computed unless cancelled, and the result scan returns the lowest failing slot; for_each_band does the same under its queue lock; outputs land at fixed positions; panics are re-raised; no unsafe. findings.evidence: With a converter, every tile of a batch (4 x threads tiles, so 4 on Threads::single and 64 on 16 threads) is converted before any stage C of that batch runs. When tile j fails in stage C, the converter has already been called for later tiles, and how many depends on the thread count. The returned error is identical, but the caller-owned converter's side effects differ: calls(), Prism plan-cache stats, Observe frames sent to the converter's sink, and ledger leases taken and released. A serial run before f132843 stopped after tile j. The parallel test asserts only the error and the calling thread, not recorder.calls on a failing run. The DESCRIPTOR claims refusals are identical for every thread count.
findings.remediation: Run stage C of a batch before converting the next tile past a failure, or document converter side effects as count-dependent

findings.evidence: inputs = usize::from(t.num_input_channels) is the untrusted u8 from the mAB tag, while moxcms LutMultidimensionalType.grid_points is [u8; 16]. moxcms only skips the tag when 'in_channels > 4 && out_channels > 4' (&&, not ||), and bounds its own grid loops with .take(in_channels) over 16 entries. An RGB profile whose A2B0 is an mAB with 17..255 inputs, 3 outputs and a CLUT (first 16 grid points 2, about 196 KB of data, inside the 2 MiB limit) therefore parses in moxcms and passes admit() (wide.rs:288-380 checks only tag types). The slice panics in Table::build before Clut::new's inputs <= 8 check and before to_pcs compares table.inputs with the device channels. Before 3926709, moxcms's own transform checked channel counts (katana md_pipeline.rs:200), so this crash is new with the Prism evaluator. tests/wide_hostile.rs covers u32-max sizes and oversized CLUTs, but not the channel count.
findings.remediation: In Table::build refuse inputs > 8 (or > grid_points.len()) before slicing; add an mAB 17-input hostile test

findings.evidence: The same descriptor says in admitted_route that AdmittedWideEngine 'charges the caller's ledger before every allocation', and still lists 'caller memory-ledger admission of the wide path (bounded by profile size, pixel limit and cache capacity)' under not_in_scope. A consumer reading not_in_scope would conclude that develop's conversion is unaccounted.
findings.remediation: Drop the not_in_scope entry or scope it to the plain WideEngine; cite tests/wide_admitted.rs in admitted_route (V4-07)

findings.evidence: The lease sizes come from reasoned factors (parse 2x stored bytes + 16 KiB, plan 8x + 16 KiB, BPC 4 x plan + ramp) and are called 'conservative upper bounds'. No test measures the real heap of a parse/plan/BPC build against the lease (develop's DNG tests show a tracking allocator is feasible). The ledger tests only check bookkeeping. An under-estimate, for example a fused plan cloning curve tables more than once, would pass silently while STU-CON-044 accounting reads as exact.
findings.remediation: Add a tracking-allocator test: peak heap of transform on a miss (incl. BPC, CMYK table) <= reserved bytes

findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-prism/src/icc_eval.rs:212-215,225 (Gamma(g) for curv count 1 or para type 0, any g), :298 (inverse root uses 1/g)
findings.evidence: A curv gamma of 0 (u8Fixed8 0) or a para type-0 gamma <= 0 is accepted. On a destination, inverse() computes pow(v, 1/g) with g = 0 or g < 0, so in-gamut values map silently to 0 (or 1/inf) instead of a typed refusal for a non-invertible curve. Types 1-4 refuse only a = 0.
findings.remediation: Refuse g <= 0 (and non-finite) for destination curves as MalformedProfile; add T0 cases

findings.evidence: When PRISM-LUT-DEST-ACCURACY-001 was closed, 8 RGB->CMYK absolute combos that still exceed the gate were re-attributed to the pending divergence DIV-ABS-V2-DISPLAY-WTPT-001. The attribution evidence (wtpt forced to D50 gives max 0.0055) comes from an uncommitted experiment, and expected-fail entries cannot fail the gate, so these 8 combos are unguarded until the lead decides the divergence.
findings.remediation: Commit the wtpt-forced-D50 variant as an asserting test, so the re-attribution is proven

findings.evidence: A proposal carries the whole successor instance, cloned from the proposer's snapshot, while its write footprint now names only the edited (instance_id, override/<node>/<field>) keys. Two proposals that edit different fields of the same instance have disjoint footprints and both admit, as STU-ARC-011 requires. But if the host commits proposal.instance as a record replacement, the second commit drops the first proposal's override (lost update). The footprint promises field-level disjointness that the payload does not express. This pre-dates ed9b130, which made the per-field keys explicit.
findings.remediation: Carry the edited fields as a delta (node, field, value) to be merged, or add (instance_id, "") to the write footprint
